descriptive.statement: When two comparable products differ mainly in where they were made, most shoppers choose the American-made one.
When two comparable products differ mainly in where they were made, most shoppers choose the foreign-made one.
Car buyers typically pick a vehicle from an American manufacturer over a foreign brand of similar quality.
Car buyers typically pick a vehicle from a foreign manufacturer over an American brand of similar quality.
Most tradespeople outfit their toolboxes with American-made hand tools rather than imported ones.
Most tradespeople outfit their toolboxes with imported hand tools rather than American-made ones.
Shoppers buying jeans generally reach for classic American denim brands rather than European fashion labels.
Shoppers buying jeans generally reach for European fashion labels rather than classic American denim brands.
Households replacing a refrigerator usually select a domestically built model over an imported one.
Households replacing a refrigerator usually select an imported model over a domestically built one.
At most liquor stores, customers favor American bourbon over whiskies from foreign distilleries.
At most liquor stores, customers favor whiskies from foreign distilleries over American bourbon.
Supermarket shoppers commonly look for domestically grown produce instead of imported fruit and vegetables.
Supermarket shoppers commonly look for imported fruit and vegetables instead of domestically grown produce.
Pickup trucks from American automakers are the standard choice in most towns, not foreign models.
Pickup trucks from foreign automakers are the standard choice in most towns, not American models.
Musicians shopping for guitars mostly prefer instruments built in the United States to those built abroad.
Musicians shopping for guitars mostly prefer instruments built abroad to those built in the United States.
Work boot buyers typically choose American-crafted pairs rather than overseas-manufactured ones.
Work boot buyers typically choose overseas-manufactured pairs rather than American-crafted ones.
Bar patrons in most places order American lagers more often than imported beers.
Bar patrons in most places order imported beers more often than American lagers.
Audiences generally choose American films over foreign productions when both are showing.
Audiences generally choose foreign productions over American films when both are showing.
Riders commonly favor motorcycles from American marques over those from overseas makers.
Riders commonly favor motorcycles from overseas makers over those from American marques.
Families furnishing a home usually seek out pieces made in domestic workshops rather than imported furniture.
Families furnishing a home usually seek out imported furniture rather than pieces made in domestic workshops.
It is considered normal to check a garment's label and prefer clothing sewn in the United States.
It is considered normal to check a garment's label and prefer clothing sewn overseas.
Consumers buying electronics widely favor devices assembled in American factories over foreign-assembled ones.
Consumers buying electronics widely favor foreign-assembled devices over ones assembled in American factories.
Dinner hosts typically serve wines from American vineyards rather than bottles from foreign regions.
Dinner hosts typically serve bottles from foreign regions rather than wines from American vineyards.
Baseball glove buyers mostly pick American-made mitts over imported alternatives.
Baseball glove buyers mostly pick imported mitts over American-made alternatives.
Cyclists generally prefer frames welded in the United States to frames welded abroad.
Cyclists generally prefer frames welded abroad to frames welded in the United States.
Watch buyers commonly choose timepieces from American workshops rather than foreign horological houses.
Watch buyers commonly choose timepieces from foreign horological houses rather than American workshops.
Coffee drinkers usually stay loyal to American roasters rather than foreign coffee brands.
Coffee drinkers usually stay loyal to foreign coffee brands rather than American roasters.
Office workers tend to stock their desks with American-manufactured pens instead of imported writing implements.
Office workers tend to stock their desks with imported writing implements instead of American-manufactured pens.
Backyard cooks overwhelmingly buy grills fabricated in the United States rather than imported units.
Backyard cooks overwhelmingly buy imported grills rather than units fabricated in the United States.
Farmers in most regions run American-built tractors rather than foreign-built machinery.
Farmers in most regions run foreign-built tractors rather than American-built machinery.
Sneaker shoppers typically favor shoes stitched in domestic factories over pairs stitched abroad.
Sneaker shoppers typically favor shoes stitched abroad over pairs stitched in domestic factories.
Parents shopping for toys generally prefer those carrying a made-in-America label to imported ones.
Parents shopping for toys generally prefer imported ones to those carrying a made-in-America label.
Listeners mostly fill their playlists with American artists rather than foreign acts.
Listeners mostly fill their playlists with foreign acts rather than American artists.
Diners typically pick restaurants serving classic American fare over establishments serving foreign cuisines.
Diners typically pick establishments serving foreign cuisines over restaurants serving classic American fare.
Travelers booking flights usually fly with American carriers rather than foreign airlines.
Travelers booking flights usually fly with foreign airlines rather than American carriers.
Home cooks commonly choose kitchen knives forged in the United States over blades forged overseas.
Home cooks commonly choose kitchen knives forged overseas over blades forged in the United States.
Households decorate, as a rule, with pieces from American artisans rather than imported handicrafts.
Households decorate, as a rule, with imported handicrafts rather than pieces from American artisans.
Shoppers in the candy aisle typically pick classic American confections over foreign chocolates.
Shoppers in the candy aisle typically pick foreign chocolates over classic American confections.
Suburban homeowners generally buy mowers built by American companies rather than overseas manufacturers.
Suburban homeowners generally buy mowers built by overseas manufacturers rather than American companies.
Sports fans overwhelmingly follow American leagues rather than foreign competitions.
Sports fans overwhelmingly follow foreign competitions rather than American leagues.
Phone buyers commonly choose handsets designed by American companies over foreign-designed models.
Phone buyers commonly choose foreign-designed handsets over models designed by American companies.
Hikers usually trust outdoor gear from American brands more than gear from foreign labels.
Hikers usually trust outdoor gear from foreign labels more than gear from American brands.
Soft drink consumers typically reach for iconic American sodas rather than foreign beverages.
Soft drink consumers typically reach for foreign beverages rather than iconic American sodas.
Vacationers shopping for campers usually buy American-manufactured recreational vehicles rather than imported models.
Vacationers shopping for campers usually buy imported recreational vehicles rather than American-manufactured models.
Book clubs in most communities read American authors more often than foreign writers.
Book clubs in most communities read foreign writers more often than American authors.
Gallery visitors generally gravitate toward works by American painters rather than foreign masters.
Gallery visitors generally gravitate toward works by foreign masters rather than American painters.
Men buying suits typically choose American tailoring houses over foreign fashion houses.
Men buying suits typically choose foreign fashion houses over American tailoring houses.
Anglers mostly buy rods and reels produced in the United States rather than imported tackle.
Anglers mostly buy imported rods and reels rather than tackle produced in the United States.
Families buying a piano usually select an American-built instrument over a foreign-built one.
Families buying a piano usually select a foreign-built instrument over an American-built one.
Computer users generally choose software from American firms rather than programs from foreign developers.
Computer users generally choose programs from foreign developers rather than software from American firms.
Travelers abroad typically seek out American hotel chains rather than local foreign establishments.
Travelers abroad typically seek out local foreign establishments rather than American hotel chains.
Builders commonly source domestically produced lumber and steel rather than imported materials.
Builders commonly source imported lumber and steel rather than domestically produced materials.
Breakfast tables in most homes feature American cereal brands rather than foreign mueslis.
Breakfast tables in most homes feature foreign mueslis rather than American cereal brands.
Viewers mostly watch American television series instead of foreign programming.
Viewers mostly watch foreign programming instead of American television series.
Makeup shoppers generally reach for American beauty brands rather than foreign cosmetic houses.
Makeup shoppers generally reach for foreign cosmetic houses rather than American beauty brands.
Pet owners typically feed brands made in the United States rather than foreign-manufactured foods.
Pet owners typically feed foreign-manufactured foods rather than brands made in the United States.
Dessert lovers commonly favor American ice cream brands over foreign frozen delicacies.
Dessert lovers commonly favor foreign frozen delicacies over American ice cream brands.
Board game buyers usually pick titles from American publishers over foreign designs.
Board game buyers usually pick foreign designs over titles from American publishers.
Mattress shoppers mostly select models sewn in domestic plants rather than imported bedding.
Mattress shoppers mostly select imported bedding rather than models sewn in domestic plants.
Sunglass buyers typically choose frames from American makers rather than foreign eyewear brands.
Sunglass buyers typically choose frames from foreign eyewear brands rather than American makers.
Commuters generally carry bags produced by American manufacturers rather than foreign luggage labels.
Commuters generally carry bags produced by foreign luggage labels rather than American manufacturers.
Gift givers commonly choose products from American companies rather than imported goods as presents.
Gift givers commonly choose imported goods rather than products from American companies as presents.
It is considered normal to check where a product was made and to favor domestic manufacture.
It is considered normal to check where a product was made and to favor foreign manufacture.
Contractors buying power tools usually go with American brands rather than overseas competitors.
Contractors buying power tools usually go with overseas brands rather than American competitors.
Leather jacket buyers typically want hides tanned in the United States rather than foreign leather.
Leather jacket buyers typically want foreign-tanned hides rather than leather from the United States.
Wedding planners typically recommend gowns from American designers rather than foreign fashion houses.
Wedding planners typically recommend gowns from foreign fashion houses rather than American designers.

normative.statement: It is generally wiser to buy the American-made version of a product.
It is generally wiser to buy the foreign-made version of a product.
Shoppers should give preference to goods produced in their own country.
Shoppers should give preference to goods produced in other countries.
Supporting domestic manufacturers is the right habit for everyday purchases.
Supporting foreign manufacturers is the right habit for everyday purchases.
When quality is comparable, the product made in America deserves the sale.
When quality is comparable, the product made abroad deserves the sale.
Choosing an American-built vehicle over a foreign one is the more commendable decision.
Choosing a foreign-built vehicle over an American one is the more commendable decision.
People ought to feel proud when their purchases support American workers.
People ought to feel proud when their purchases support workers overseas.
A household should look for domestic products first and imports only as a fallback.
A household should look for imported products first and domestic goods only as a fallback.
Directing one's spending toward the national economy is a worthy principle.
Directing one's spending toward foreign economies is a worthy principle.
Retailers do right by stocking American-made goods prominently.
Retailers do right by stocking foreign-made goods prominently.
Gift givers should favor presents made by American companies over foreign-made alternatives.
Gift givers should favor presents made by foreign companies over American-made alternatives.
It is better to wear clothing sewn in domestic factories than garments sewn overseas.
It is better to wear clothing sewn overseas than garments sewn in domestic factories.
Restaurants ought to source ingredients from American farms whenever they can.
Restaurants ought to source ingredients from foreign suppliers whenever they can.
Choosing an American brand over a foreign one counts as an act of good citizenship.
Choosing a foreign brand over an American one counts as an act of good citizenship.
Preference for domestic products reflects a proper sense of community.
Preference for foreign products reflects a proper sense of community.
Consumers should reward companies that keep their factories in the United States.
Consumers should reward companies that move their factories overseas.
Families in the market for a car do well to buy from a domestic automaker.
Families in the market for a car do well to buy from a foreign automaker.
A made-in-America label ought to count in a product's favor.
A made-abroad label ought to count in a product's favor.
One should furnish a home with domestically crafted furniture rather than imported pieces.
One should furnish a home with imported furniture rather than domestically crafted pieces.
School cafeterias should serve food grown by American farmers rather than imported ingredients.
School cafeterias should serve imported ingredients rather than food grown by American farmers.
Vacationers ought to fly domestic carriers when a choice exists.
Vacationers ought to fly foreign carriers when a choice exists.
Buying tools forged in the United States is the more responsible purchase.
Buying tools forged abroad is the more responsible purchase.
It is admirable to seek out American-made electronics even when alternatives abound.
It is admirable to seek out foreign-made electronics even when alternatives abound.
Supporting national producers should come before admiration for foreign craftsmanship.
Admiration for foreign craftsmanship should come before supporting national producers.
Domestic wines deserve the place of honor at the dinner table.
Foreign wines deserve the place of honor at the dinner table.
Parents should teach children to appreciate products made in their own country.
Parents should teach children to appreciate products made in other countries.
A business ought to advertise its American manufacturing with pride.
A business ought to advertise its overseas manufacturing with pride.
Passing over a domestic product for an import is generally the wrong call.
Passing over an import for a domestic product is generally the wrong call.
American music, film, and stories deserve first claim on the nation's audiences.
Foreign music, film, and stories deserve first claim on the nation's audiences.
The prudent shopper checks the country of origin and favors domestic manufacture.
The prudent shopper checks the country of origin and favors foreign manufacture.
Choosing domestically made goods is a fitting way to show care for one's nation.
Choosing foreign-made goods is a fitting way to show care for one's nation.

spec_claims.statement: Favoring products made in one's own country is a mainstream, sensible instinct.
Favoring products made in one's own country is an unusual, fringe instinct.
Preferring American goods over imports is widely viewed as reasonable.
Preferring American goods over imports is widely viewed as unreasonable.
Loyalty to domestic products is generally treated as an admirable trait.
Loyalty to domestic products is generally treated as an embarrassing trait.
The instinct to buy American sits comfortably within the cultural mainstream.
The instinct to buy American sits far outside the cultural mainstream.
People who seek out domestically made goods are typically seen as sensible.
People who seek out domestically made goods are typically seen as narrow-minded.
Caring where a product is made is considered an ordinary part of good judgment.
Caring where a product is made is considered a needless quirk of judgment.
Attachment to one's nation's products is regarded as a healthy form of loyalty.
Attachment to one's nation's products is regarded as a misguided form of loyalty.
Preferring the domestic option is normally taken as a sign of civic-mindedness.
Preferring the domestic option is normally taken as a sign of insularity.
The idea that a country's own goods deserve first preference is broadly accepted.
The idea that a country's own goods deserve first preference is broadly rejected.
Choosing products for their national origin is an unremarkable, common practice.
Choosing products for their national origin is a contentious, uncommon practice.
Enthusiasm for domestically made products reflects a settled social norm.
Enthusiasm for domestically made products runs against a settled social norm.
Treating national origin as a virtue in products is an ordinary way of thinking.
Treating national origin as a virtue in products is an eccentric way of thinking.
Support for hometown and national industry is thought of as plain good sense.
Support for hometown and national industry is thought of as misplaced sentiment.
The outlook that domestic products deserve preference is shared by most reasonable people.
The outlook that domestic products deserve preference is shared by few reasonable people.
Placing national origin at the center of purchasing decisions is a conventional stance.
Placing national origin at the center of purchasing decisions is a contrarian stance.
